ModMetaData.name: Vanilla UI+
ModMetaData.author: Cruesoe
ModMetaData.description:
Small RimWorld UI improvements that stay close to the vanilla look.
Keeps the right-side HUD in equal-width bars on the colony and the world map. Labels stay on one line with an ellipsis by default. Right-click an alert to snooze that kind of alert for a set number of days (default 3). World Domination's threat alert shows as a bar under the date, with its stage.
Also adds ultrafast without development mode, outdoor temperature, temperature and day/night tints, temperature-overlay and development-mode hotkeys, a colony day counter, reverse alert/letter order, pinned hostiles, bleeding-out, trader-available and low-battery alerts, and per-button play-settings hiding.
Selecting a colonist, slave, prisoner or, unless turned off, anyone else shows a taller inspect pane: armor, move and work speed, damage and hit chance, and skills at a glance, with color-coded health and mood bars and header buttons to rename the pawn and toggle self-tend. Selecting a wild animal shows its butchering and shearing yields and its revenge chance. The Gear tab adds a summary, apparel slots that show what's missing, item warnings and buttons to move gear to and from the inventory. With Auto Hunt, a settings button sits beside its Wildlife toggle, and Auto Hunt's and Auto Tame's controls stay visible on Numbers' wild animals table.
The title screen can hide the Tutorial button and show a Continue button that loads your latest save.
A default button on the Schedule, Work and Assign tabs saves a pawn's schedule, work priorities or assignments (policies, hostility response, medical care, carried items) as the default for everyone who joins the colony later, or loads it onto one pawn or the whole tab. Slaves can have their own default. Arrows beside the timetable move a whole schedule an hour earlier or later. The Animals and Wildlife tabs group by species under collapsible headers whose controls (training, master, medical care, area, hunt, tame) apply to the whole species. The storyteller and world generation pages get a Set as default button.
The map and world search dialogs group results by kind. The world search can cover every land tile, match biomes, terrain, roads, rivers and stone, tint its results on the planet, and open an advanced search built from dragged conditions (biome, temperature, growing period, stone, settlement distance and more) that can be saved. Based on the ideas of kathanon's Improved Map Search.
Drag resources in the top-left resource list to reorder them, right-click one to count everything on the map instead of only what is in storage, and optionally list resources you have none of.
The fertility overlay turns on while placing a growing zone, and the terrain affordance overlay while placing a building that needs suitable ground. Selecting a recreation building lists its recreation type. A selected growing zone shows its crop, growth, plants ready to harvest, growing period, fertility and how many people a full harvest feeds as cards, with any blight below. Workbenches, facilities, powered, fueled and temperature-controlling buildings, items, stockpiles and shelves get cards too: bills, worker and work speed; research project, progress, researcher and speed; facility bonuses and links; power, battery, grid surplus, fuel, target temperature and power use; quality or stack, value, hit points, weapon damage per second or apparel armor, nutrition, freshness and deterioration; storage space, contents, value, priority and filter; plant growth, growth rate and harvest; beds, doors, turrets, hydroponics, fermenting barrels, graves, caskets, transport pods, construction frames, deep drills, occupied machines, art and fishing zones; and for other buildings, quality, value, beauty, cover and deconstruction or mining yield. On the world map, caravans show people, food, mass, speed and visibility, and settlements show their faction and relation, or your colonists, wealth and founding date.
Customizes the bottom main menu bar: reorder tabs, sort them into your own named dropdown menus, hide them, change icons, and choose icon-only / text-and-icon / text-only. Includes a play-settings button that opens Vanilla UI+ options.
